plain_description.what: Rebuilds the tree learned without topic labels (the anchor-free tree) with smaller minimum cell sizes (40 and 30 questions instead of 55). It then compares the number of leaves, label purity, how many splits pass the certificate, and how many held-out questions each leaf gets. No judge calls.
plain_description.why: Checks whether the anchor-free tree could split further, and what finer cells would cost.
plain_description.information: If smaller cells keep quality and still have enough questions, finer cells could be used. If they leave too few questions per cell, the registered size of 55 stays. Result: exploratory only, so it settles nothing. Smaller cells give more leaves (81, then 108, then 143) and slightly higher purity. They lower the share of certified splits and leave very few questions per cell (median 20 at size 30, as few as 6), far below the roughly 120-190 needed. Size 55 stays.
